      <h1>Our Own Cost Spread — Measuring the Variance Before We Budget</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">A one-page variance exhibit in our own numbers — the CFO-facing artifact that reframes the agentic bill from a price negotiation into an engineering-design decision.</p>
      <p style="font-size:12pt;font-weight:700;margin:1mm 0 0">Model choice, token use and harness govern the bill, and all three are in our control.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-07-cost-variance-baseline</b><br>
      Pack C - The case and the money<br>
      fill order <b>4</b> &middot; type <b>calculator</b><br>
      audience <b>mixed</b>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-source">

    &middot; <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch07-the-agentic-sdlc-bill.html#sec-bill-cost-variance">#sec-bill-cost-variance</a>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    Choose up to three recurring, high-frequency engineering tasks. For each task, record your own run count, describe both loops, enter your own costs, and mark each cost basis separately. Record whether outputs are identical, calculate the spread and exposure, and name the individual who would own the design of this path. Mark the measurement window. Use only your organization's figures; do not copy the illustrative run. If every cost basis is estimated, mark the sheet PROSPECTIVE. Circle the highest-spread task and carry it into WS-07-three-variables-audit; carry total annualized exposure into WS-07-spend-pool-budget-model.

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>Book's illustrative run
      <span class="ws-block-note">reference only; not an organization figure</span></h2>
    <div class="prior--hedged">
      <span class="hedge-figure">One illustrative run on a nineteen-file refactor cost $41.01 undesigned and $4.81 designed — an 8.5× spread on identical output.</span>
      <span class="hedge-text">The figures in this chapter -- the 8.5x spread, the $4.81 versus $41.01 run, the model-price ranges -- are <b>illustrative single runs and point-in-time prices</b>, not benchmarks. They are real, and they are not universal: the magnitude depends on the task, the models available the week you read this, and the harness. Treat them as existence proofs of <i>variance you can engineer</i>, not as a guaranteed return. The durable claim is the mechanism — model choice, token use, and harness govern the bill, and all three are in your control. The specific multiples will move. The lever will not.</span>
      <span class="hedge-src">handbook/ch07-the-agentic-sdlc-bill.qmd L13, L118</span>
    </div>
  </div>
